F1: Closing any strategy shuts down the factory’s shared pool, so later assignments can silently mark unprocessed messages complete.
F2: The test’s no-commit assertion contradicts the completion behavior and can fail when a commit tick occurs during its timing window.
F3: The gap assertions assume missing Kafka offsets block commits, but the tracker skips holes and the timing checks can fail on a later commit tick.
F4: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure and can grow until they exhaust process memory when processing falls behind.
F5: Shutdown may abandon queued work, but those offsets remain uncommitted and Kafka can redeliver it; the remaining concern is documentation and shutdown latency.
F6: Workers can drain the queue before the stats assertion, making the test flaky.
